declared.title: Lost in the Mall? Interrogating Judgements of False Memory
declared.foundIn: dossier draft memory-rewritten (keptOut) and reports/memory-rewritten/counter-evidence.md (card 9); OpenAlex search « lost in the mall reanalysis transcripts false memories investigator judgements participants », from 2024 (2026-11-26)

population: transcripts of the Irish participants of murphy-2023-mall whom the researchers had judged to have a false memory

findings.text: In that replication, the researchers' judgements counted many more false memories than the participants themselves reported

support.sentence: In this new study standard investigator judgements indicated many more false memories than did participants themselves, consistent with similar studies.

findings.text: Of six suggested core details, fewer than two were recalled on average; 20% of « full » and 58% of « partial » false memories did not include being lost

support.sentence: On average, fewer than two details in the fake event were explicitly recalled; 20% with full and 58% with partial false memories did not recall being lost.

findings.text: Half the participants described experiences that may be true, distinct from the made-up event

support.sentence: Half the participants described potentially true experiences, distinguishable from the fake event; this group recalled more suggested details but tended to remember them differently.

limits: by the authors of brewin-2017-childhood, one side of a published debate; Murphy & Greene replied in 2025 (10.1002/acp.70044): even 4% would matter
a new coding of one study's transcripts (123 people, Ireland), not new data: classed as cross-sectional
